text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In a lecture to army officers in Abuja, former head of state retired Major-General Muhammed Buhari says he seized power in 1983 to clean the nation of corruption but was unfortunately "cleansed out himself" in a coup 20 months later.

- Buhari, who now heads Petroleum Trust Fund (PTF) charged with rehabilitating public infrastructure from proceeds of 1994 pump price hike says he will not transfer to central bank nearly 30 billion naira of the fund's money now in commercial banks.
- Banking sources say PTF has started gradual withdrawal of its deposits from banks with about 11 billion recalled last week in a bid to reduce excess liquidity in the market.
- Oil workers union NUPENG dispels rumour of strike over dispute between road tanker drivers and owners of the vehicles.
- PTF has up to date received 70.43 billion naira, says its chairman Buhari, who alleges that there is a strong plot by "powerful" forces to get the fund scrapped.
- Campaigns for local council election on Saturday stepped up with candidates moving in carnival-like motorcades from ward to ward.

- Radical opposition lawyer Gani Fawehinmi briefed to take over case of 19 Ogoni youths facing charges of murder of four chiefs which led to hanging in 1995 of nine minority rights activists including author Ken Saro-Wiwa.
- Staff of container terminal at Lagos port embark on strike against what they term unfavourable working conditions.
- Political parties search for 256 fresh candidates for Saturday's local council poll following disqualification by electoral commission of some of the candidates they presented.
- Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas Company seeks fresh market in Portugal for gas that will be rolled out from 1999.
